title: Division 7A — payments, loans and forgiven debts treated as dividends
summary: Division 7A treats certain payments, loans and forgiven debts by a private company to a shareholder or associate as unfrankable dividends unless an exception applies. The flowchart covers the trigger provisions (ss 109C, 109D, 109F), the shareholder/associate nexus, the Subdivision D exceptions (ss 109J-109NA), the loan-repaid-before-lodgment day carve-out (s 109D(1)(b)), amalgamated loans (s 109E), the distributable surplus cap (s 109Y), franking and character consequences (ss 109Z-109ZB), interposed entities (ss 109T-109U), the trust UPE limb (s 109XA), and Commissioner discretion (s 109RB). Subsection coverage: ss 109C-109ZE mapped to nodes.

nodes.label: A private company makes a payment, loan, or forgives a debt to an entity
nodes.body: Division 7A may treat the amount as an unfrankable dividend if the entity is a shareholder or associate and no exception applies. The three triggers are: payment to an entity (s 109C), loan to an entity (s 109D), and forgiveness of all or part of a debt owed to the company (s 109F). Payment includes the provision of an asset for use (s 109CA).

nodes.label: What type of dealing with the private company?
nodes.body: Three triggers: (1) a payment made to the entity during the income year (s 109C); (2) a loan made to the entity during the income year (s 109D); or (3) all or part of a debt owed to the company is forgiven (s 109F). Each triggers a deemed dividend only if the shareholder/associate nexus is satisfied and no Subdivision D exception applies.

nodes.label: Payment made to an entity during the income year (s 109C)
nodes.body: A private company is taken to pay a dividend to an entity at the end of the income year if the company pays an amount to the entity during the year and the entity is a shareholder or associate at the time of payment, or a reasonable person would conclude the payment is made because the entity has been such a shareholder or associate (s 109C(1)(a)-(b)). Payment includes provision of an asset for use (s 109CA). Some payments are excluded by Subdivision D (ss 109J-109NA).

nodes.label: Loan made to an entity during the income year (s 109D)
nodes.body: A private company is taken to pay a dividend to an entity at the end of the income year if: (a) the company makes a loan to the entity during the current year; (b) the loan is not fully repaid before the lodgment day for the current year; (c) Subdivision D does not prevent the deemed dividend; and (d) the entity is a shareholder or associate (s 109D(1)(a)-(d)). 'Loan' includes an advance of money, provision of credit or financial accommodation, a payment with an obligation to repay, and any transaction that in substance effects a loan (s 109D(3)).

nodes.label: Debt owed to the private company is forgiven (s 109F)
nodes.body: A private company is taken to pay a dividend to an entity at the end of the income year if all or part of a debt the entity owed the company is forgiven in that year and either: (a) the amount is forgiven when the entity is a shareholder or associate; or (b) a reasonable person would conclude the amount is forgiven because the entity has been such a shareholder or associate (s 109F(1)(a)-(b)). In some cases forgiving a debt does not give rise to a dividend — see s 109G.

nodes.label: Is the entity a shareholder or an associate of a shareholder, or is the dealing because of that capacity?
nodes.body: The shareholder/associate nexus must be satisfied for all three triggers. For payments (s 109C(1)(a)-(b)) and loans (s 109D(1)(d)(i)-(ii)): the entity must be a shareholder or associate at the time, or a reasonable person would conclude the dealing is because the entity has been such a shareholder or associate. For forgiven debts (s 109F(1)(a)-(b)): same test. Section 109ZE provides interpretation rules about entities. Section 109ZE defines 'associate' by reference to s 109ZE read with the entity rules in s 960-100 of ITAA 1997.

nodes.label: Loan path: Is the loan fully repaid before the lodgment day?
nodes.body: A loan is only treated as a dividend under s 109D(1) if it is not fully repaid before the lodgment day for the current year (s 109D(1)(b)). If fully repaid by that date, no deemed dividend arises under s 109D(1). Note that some payments relating to loans are not taken into account for working out how much has been repaid — see s 109R.

nodes.label: Loan fully repaid before lodgment day — no deemed dividend under s 109D(1)
nodes.body: If the loan is fully repaid before the lodgment day for the current year, s 109D(1) does not apply. However, certain repayments may be disregarded under s 109R. Also, if the loan was made in the course of winding-up and not repaid, s 109D(1A) may apply in the following year.

nodes.label: Does a Subdivision D exception apply?
nodes.body: Subdivision D (ss 109J-109NA) contains exceptions that prevent payments or loans from being treated as dividends. The exceptions are: discharging a pecuniary obligation at arm's length (s 109J); inter-company payments and loans (s 109K); amounts already assessable or excluded by another provision (s 109L); loans in the ordinary course of business on arm's length terms (s 109M); loans meeting minimum interest rate and maximum term criteria with a written agreement (s 109N); and certain liquidator's distributions and loans (s 109NA). For forgiven debts, see also s 109G (not within Subdiv D).

nodes.label: Exception applies — no deemed dividend
nodes.body: If any Subdivision D exception applies, the payment or loan is not treated as a dividend under s 109C or s 109D. For loans made in winding-up (s 109NA), if the loan is not fully repaid by the end of the following year, it may be treated as a dividend under s 109D(1A).

nodes.label: Calculate the deemed dividend amount
nodes.body: For payments (s 109C): the amount paid is the dividend, subject to s 109Y. For loans (s 109D(1AA)): the amount of the dividend is the amount of the loan that has not been repaid before the lodgment day, subject to s 109Y. For forgiven debts (s 109F): the amount forgiven is the dividend, subject to s 109Y. If the loan was made in a previous year and the minimum yearly repayment is not met, an amalgamated loan shortfall is treated as a dividend under s 109E.

nodes.label: Is there an amalgamated loan from a previous year with a shortfall in the minimum yearly repayment?
nodes.body: An amalgamated loan from an earlier year is treated as a dividend at the end of the current year if: (a) the amalgamated loan is not repaid at the end of the current year; and (b) the amount paid during the year falls short of the minimum yearly repayment worked out under s 109E(5). The shortfall amount is the deemed dividend, subject to s 109Y. This applies in addition to any current-year loan.

nodes.label: Cap the total deemed dividends to the distributable surplus (s 109Y)
nodes.body: If the sum of all dividends the company is taken to pay under Division 7A at the end of the income year would exceed the company's distributable surplus, each dividend is proportionally reduced (s 109Y(1)). The distributable surplus is calculated as: net assets + Division 7A amounts - non-commercial loans - paid-up share value - repayments of non-commercial loans (s 109Y(2)). This cap applies to ALL deemed dividends under the Division.

nodes.label: Apply franking and character consequences (ss 109Z-109ZB)
nodes.body: A deemed dividend under Division 7A is taken to be paid to the entity as a shareholder (s 109Z(a)) and out of the company's profits (s 109Z(b)). It is disregarded for withholding tax purposes (s 109ZA). The amount treated as a dividend is not a fringe benefit (s 109ZB). The dividend is unfrankable under s 202-45(g) of ITAA 1997 — it cannot be franked, except where s 109RB or s 109RC allows franking.

nodes.label: Is the dealing through an interposed entity or guarantee arrangement?
nodes.body: Division 7A extends to arrangements involving interposed entities. If a private company makes a payment or loan to an interposed entity as part of an arrangement involving a payment or loan to a target shareholder/associate, the Division operates as if the company made the payment or loan directly to the target (s 109T). Similarly, if the company guarantees a loan made by another entity as part of such an arrangement (s 109U).

nodes.label: Trust UPE limb: Has the trustee made a payment, loan or forgiven a debt to a shareholder of a private company with an unpaid present entitlement?
nodes.body: Subdivision EA (s 109XA) applies where a trustee makes a payment (or loan or debt forgiveness) to a shareholder or associate of a private company, and the payment discharges or reduces a present entitlement of the shareholder that is wholly or partly attributable to an unrealised gain. If triggered, s 109XB deems a dividend paid by the private company. This is the 'trust UPE' limb of Division 7A.

nodes.label: Commissioner may disregard the operation of the Division or allow franking (s 109RB)
nodes.body: If Division 7A would operate to treat an amount as a dividend, the Commissioner may make a decision under s 109RB(2) to disregard the operation of the Division (in whole or part) or allow the dividend to be franked. This discretion applies where the Commissioner considers it fair and reasonable having regard to: the extent of the shareholder's interest, the quantum of the deemed dividend, any distributions made, and other relevant circumstances (s 109RB(1)-(4)).

nodes.label: Franking allowed for family law obligations (s 109RC)
nodes.body: If a dividend is taken to be paid under Division 7A because of a family law obligation, the unfrankability rule in s 202-45(g)(i) of ITAA 1997 does not apply. The dividend can be franked at the company's benchmark franking percentage for the franking period (s 109RC(1)-(3)).

nodes.label: Deemed dividend applies — assessable to shareholder as unfranked dividend
nodes.body: The amount is included in the shareholder's assessable income as an unfranked dividend under s 44(1) of ITAA 1936, capped at the distributable surplus. The private company must account for franking debits. Review options: the Commissioner may exercise discretion under s 109RB or the taxpayer may object under Part IVC.

nodes.label: No deemed dividend under Division 7A
nodes.body: The dealing does not give rise to a deemed dividend under Division 7A. This may be because: the entity was not a shareholder or associate, the loan was fully repaid before lodgment day, a Subdivision D exception applied, the distributable surplus was nil, or the Commissioner exercised discretion under s 109RB. The dealing is assessed under ordinary principles if applicable.

nodes.label: No Division 7A trigger — dealing outside scope
nodes.body: The dealing does not fall within any of the three triggers (payment, loan, forgiven debt) or the shareholder/associate nexus is not satisfied. No deemed dividend arises under Division 7A. The transaction may still be assessed under other provisions of the income tax law.
